name: cd

name: pwd
description: Print working directory - shows current directory path

name: mkdir
description: Create new directories

name: touch
description: Create empty files or update file timestamps

flags.description: Do not create the file if it does not exist
Use the given date instead of now (GNU)
Use the timestamps of file ref

examples.description: Create an empty file (or update its modification time)

name: cp
description: Copy files and directories

flags.description: Archive mode: copy recursively and preserve permissions, ownership, timestamps and symlinks

name: mv
description: Move or rename files and directories
notes: mv overwrites an existing destination file without asking unless you pass -i or -n

name: ln

name: find
description: Search for files and directories in a directory hierarchy

flags.description: Find files modified n days ago
Run a command on the matched files

examples.description: Find all .txt files in current directory and subdirectories

notes: Very powerful when combined with -exec to perform actions on found files
WARNING: -delete and -exec rm are irreversible; always run the same find without them first to check the matches

name: tree
description: Display a directory's contents as an indented tree

flags.description: Limit the depth of the tree
Exclude files matching pattern (use | for multiple)

examples.description: Show two levels of the current directory
Show a project tree excluding common build folders

name: rmdir

systemd timers are a modern alternative with logging via journalctl

name: dmesg
description: Print kernel messages: hardware, drivers, OOM kills and disk errors

flags.description: Human-friendly output with a pager and colours

examples.description: Recent kernel messages with readable times
Check whether the OOM killer stopped a process
Watch messages live (e.g. while plugging in a USB device)

notes: Many distros restrict dmesg to root (kernel.dmesg_restrict=1), hence sudo
journalctl -k shows the same kernel messages, including from previous boots with -b -1

name: apt
description: Install, upgrade and remove packages on Debian and Ubuntu

examples.command: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade
examples.description: Refresh package lists, then install available upgrades
Remove a package but keep its system config files (purge removes those too)
Remove dependencies that are no longer needed
Show version, size, dependencies and description

notes: apt is meant for interactive use; in scripts and Dockerfiles use apt-get, whose output format is stable
full-upgrade (dist-upgrade in apt-get) may remove packages to resolve dependency changes; review the list before confirming

name: dnf
description: Install, upgrade and remove packages on Fedora, RHEL, Rocky and AlmaLinux

examples.description: Find which package ships a file or command

notes: Fedora 41+ uses DNF5 as dnf; RHEL-based distros may still ship DNF 4, where these commands work the same way
yum is a compatibility alias for dnf on modern systems

name: echo
description: Print text or variable values to standard output

flags.description: Do not print the trailing newline

examples.description: Append a line to a file
Show the exit code of the last command

notes: > overwrites a file, >> appends
echo's handling of -e and escapes differs between shells; use printf for portable formatted output
Single quotes prevent variable expansion; double quotes allow it

name: export
description: Set an environment variable for the current shell and its child processes

examples.description: Export all variables defined in a .env file

notes: Variables only last for the current session; add export lines to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc to persist them
No spaces around = (export A = b is an error)
Avoid exporting secrets in shell history; prefix the command with a space if HISTCONTROL=ignorespace is set

name: env
description: Print the environment or run a command with a modified environment

flags.description: Remove a variable from the environment

examples.description: Run a single command with an extra variable
Start a shell with a clean environment

notes: '#!/usr/bin/env bash' in scripts finds the interpreter via PATH, making scripts portable
printenv NAME prints a single variable

name: which
description: Show the full path of the executable that would run for a command

flags.description: Show all matching executables in PATH

examples.description: Show every node binary on the PATH
Show whether a name is an alias, function, builtin, or file (bash/zsh)
POSIX-portable way to check if a command exists (good in scripts)

notes: which does not know about shell aliases or functions; use type for that
In scripts prefer 'command -v' since which's behaviour varies between systems

name: alias
description: Create shortcuts for commands in your shell

examples.description: Create an alias for a long listing
Run the original command, bypassing an alias

notes: Aliases only last for the current session; add them to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc to persist
Aliases cannot take arguments in the middle; use a shell function for that

name: history
description: Show and reuse previously run shell commands

flags.description: Clear the history list for the current session (bash)

notes: Press Ctrl+R for interactive reverse search
History is saved to ~/.bash_history or ~/.zsh_history when the shell exits
Commands containing secrets end up in history; prefix them with a space when HISTCONTROL=ignorespace (bash) or setopt HIST_IGNORE_SPACE (zsh) is set
